context: Responsive multi-breakpoint scatter plot of iris morphometrics with three layouts: wide (scatter + marginal histograms), medium (simplified scatter), and narrow (strip plot + box overlays)
first_impression: Structurally honest encoding with good use of scaleSqrt for radius and data-driven domains, but the screenshot shows a blank chart (only x-axis visible), indicating a rendering/timing failure at capture.
what_works: scaleSqrt correctly used for circle radius in wide layout avoiding lie factor; xDomain/yDomain derived from d3.extent rather than hardcoded magic numbers; key function d => d.id on data joins prevents corruption across layout transitions; histogram bars correctly drawn from zero baseline.
what_doesnt: Histogram bin thresholds are hardcoded arbitrary counts (24 and 20) rather than data-driven rules like Sturges or Scott, introducing potential binning bias; the screenshot captures a blank chart with only the x-axis rendered, suggesting dots enter with opacity 0 and the transition animation was not complete at capture time, a robustness gap in initial render.
